title: Prove exact subsequence counts for XOR layouts (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped all-size combinatorial proof, with finite corroboration. For the ordered XOR permutation on n-bit addresses, the exact number of longest decreasing index subsequences is

`2^(sum_{i: m_i=0} 2^(number of one bits above i))`.

The complete length enumerator follows this exact recurrence:

```text
f = 1 + t
for each mask bit, from least to most significant:
    zero: f = 2*f - 1
    one:  f = f*f
```

At width two, masks `01` and `10` both have maximum decreasing length two, but have exactly two and four longest subsequences. The new result counts multiplicities and every subsequence length. Mark (Matarener)'s #3825 length/pass-model theorem and James Reed's #3831 finite length/composition evidence are cited predecessors, not audit deliverables. No literature-priority claim is intended for the elementary decomposition. This contribution is produced by Nick Petalas.

## Evidence

Before, the cited length statistic did not distinguish those masks. The new written highest-bit proof gives the exact all-size enumerator and leading coefficient. Independent endpoint/length counting, complete small index-subset enumeration, and a separate Fenwick length/count algorithm agree on all registered cases:

- 255 full polynomials at widths 0 through 7.
- 1,050,698 index subsets at widths 0 through 4.
- 2,047 longest-count cases at widths 0 through 10.
- Seven invalid-input controls and three semantic controls pass.

Both warning-strict normal and optimized direct checks passed locally in about 1.2 seconds each. Registered metadata, provenance and both commands passed together in 2.58 seconds. The generated receipt binds all six source/metadata files. Committed-byte/source-history preflight passes on `e3498bbf801dc81d5c776fded04114ce4a75bd8f`, covering all seven package files and canonical base `624de9dc66858af0945e5f8a0942488d62280d43`. Official committed export/integrity checks and a Git-free optimized replay pass. Changed source, changed numeric receipt and Boolean-for-integer receipt controls reject; all eight exported files, including the export manifest, are preserved.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/xor-subsequence-enumerator
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/xor-subsequence-enumerator --check-source-history
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/xor-subsequence-enumerator/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/xor-subsequence-enumerator/verify.py
```

Any CPython 3.12 interpreter can replace the local absolute path. Standard library only. The direct verifier also runs from the standalone package export. Proof, scope and exact input provenance are in `research/xor-subsequence-enumerator/README.md`, `TASK.json` and `SOURCES.json`.

Canonical [CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19133705). Live open PRs and claims, merged searches and distinctive main README searches were checked before claiming and committing. The cached remote scan covers 379 open PRs and 3,852 Discussion records; sparse local notes and unpublished work are outside complete coverage. Search absence is not a novelty certificate.

## Limitations

Multiplicity alone improves no split/merge pass bound. No physical routing schedule, native cost reduction, new multitape lower bound, supplier admission, new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed. Native realization, stock, restoration, precision, recursive cost and outer admission remain unrun and unpriced. No independent human review or formal proof-kernel acceptance is claimed. The polynomial implementation caps width at ten bits; the written theorem covers every finite width.

The historical card's baseline raises `KeyError: 'bit_lower'` against the current selected schema. The current `research_selected_baseline.py` source-binding control passes. This orientation mismatch is unrelated to the new mathematical checks.

## Open next questions

Can these subsequence choices count or construct minimum monotone-run partitions for a fixed XOR layout? Specify the ordered-tape/pass contract, then enumerate all masks at width three. A precise physical partition and its complete cost are the current blockers. Research stops at this first proved enumerative result.

## Related open work

The pre-DONE refresh inspected all 48 open PRs on this account, including seven created since the CLAIM. None of the other six studies XOR-layout subsequence multiplicity or this exact enumerator. No related numerical disagreement was found in that coverage, and no extra predecessor computation was run. The merged predecessors remain #3825 and #3831.

CI success is finite replay evidence, not formal proof-kernel or full multiplication-theorem acceptance. No Lean, Docker, selected cold replay or historical suite was run.

## Merge Danger

**Blast Radius:** package. Seven new files; shared scripts, frozen evidence and the selected frontier are unchanged.
